findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - An existing repo adopts Forge with one recent merged pull request that had no check runs, followed by 19 pull requests whose measured CI times are all 12 minutes. `_measure` returns `None` for the untimed pull request, and this condition suppresses the warning for the entire history. The plan calls for the median over pull requests with a time, so the available slow runs should still produce a warning. This is a pull request with no timing data, not an incomplete GitHub response page.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - GitHub reports a 45-minute test group as `cancelled` at its configured time limit. The existing timeout rule in `src/forge/checks.py:337` recognizes that result as a timeout, but `_eligible` always discards it. Close can consequently report only the short gate job as the slowest job and omit the 45 minutes, while doctor also loses that timing. This happens even when the tested commit and workflow are available locally, unlike the accepted missing-workflow case.
findings.title: Include cancelled jobs that reached their time limit

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A previous push took 12 minutes; after a fix is pushed, one new group fails after a minute while another is still running. Selecting the largest completed duration returns the previous push, so close reports its jobs and no running-job count. The current failed job and the job still running are absent, although the owner requested that information when close refuses early.
findings.title: Report the current failure when an earlier push was slower

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - Forge's generated workflow runs `python .forge/review-tests.py` in its `parent-tests` step and runs a separate `docs-check` job before the test groups (`src/forge/prcheck.py:61` and `:103`). GitHub uses the command as an unnamed step's name. The substring classifier puts `review-tests.py` under tests, and the caller passes only the slowest job to `_stages`, excluding `docs-check`. Thus ordinary Forge runs report selection as unavailable and inflate test time, even though GitHub supplied the selection timings. The test uses a fabricated `Select tests` step, so it does not expose this failure.
findings.title: Classify the generated workflow's selection time

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - `docs-check` takes 3 minutes and a dependent test group takes 9 minutes with no queue. The group is created after `docs-check`, so subtracting only the group's creation time from its completion time gives 9 minutes and suppresses its over-budget line, although its CI path took 12 minutes. The generated dependency is in `src/forge/prcheck.py:82`; the budget calculation needs the selection job as well as the group's own stages.
findings.title: Include the prerequisite selection job in each group's budget

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - In a private repo on GitHub-hosted runners, six jobs lasting 61 seconds each are reported as 6.1 runner minutes, although GitHub accounts for 12 minutes by rounding each job up. The plan specifies that per-run rounding, but this code sums raw seconds and the new test locks in a fractional total. The resulting figure understates the usage a client sees in GitHub billing. [GitHub's runner pricing](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing) describes the per-job rounding.
findings.title: Round runner usage for each job

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A behavior-preserving change that adds whitespace to the GraphQL filter, or obtains all attempts through another GitHub endpoint, fails this test solely because it searches for one exact query string. The GitHub stub returns the supplied attempts regardless of the request, so the output assertions do not independently establish that the request retrieves them. Make the fake enforce the external request's behavior and verify the resulting timing through close.
